title: grid
body:
## grid

Creates a flat rectangular grid of xSegments by ySegments quads in the local XY plane (z = 0), width along X and height along Y, centred on centre, with face normals along +Z. It is a single-sided surface with no thickness; choose it over plane when later deformation (bend, twist, shrinkwrap, smooth) needs interior vertices.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- Add solidify when the grid must have a thickness or a closed volume.
- The adaptor's recorded native qualification cases cover only a material on a cube; this operation relies on repository examples, not on a recorded qualification case.

Native binding: `grid`. Output kind: `["data"]`.

| Input port | Multiplicity | Required | Kind |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `material` | one node | yes | `material` |

| Option | Meaning | Type / constraints | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `width` | Extent of the grid along local X, centred on centre. | `{"type":"number","minimum":0,"exclusiveMinimum":true}` | `2` |
| `height` | Extent of the grid along local Y, centred on centre. | `{"type":"number","minimum":0,"exclusiveMinimum":true}` | `2` |
| `xSegments` | Number of quads along X; the grid has xSegments + 1 vertices per row. More segments let bend, twist, shrinkwrap or smooth follow curves more closely. | `{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"maximum":256}` | `10` |
| `ySegments` | Number of quads along Y; the grid has ySegments + 1 rows of vertices. | `{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"maximum":256}` | `10` |
| `centre` | World position [x, y, z] of the grid's centre. Schemaxis assigns it as the object's location, so the mesh itself stays about the local origin and later modifiers that work about that origin (mirror, bend, twist) use this point. | `{"type":"array","items":{"type":"number"},"minItems":3,"maxItems":3}` | `[0,0,0]` |
| `smoothShading` | When true, every face of the generated grid is marked smooth so Blender interpolates normals and the tessellated surface renders without visible facets; when false the faces render flat. Geometry and vertex positions are identical either way. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `false` |
